newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Omnitel to invest 600 billion lire in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Omnitel to invest 600 billion lire in 1997.

text.p: Italy's second GSM mobile phone network operator Omnitel said it intended to invest 600 billion lire ($370 million) in 1997 and boost its coverage of the Italian market to 70 percent by the end of the year.

"The board unanimously approved the strategic plans for 1997 which among other things envisage more than 600 billion lire of investments to continue to boost coverage and sustain the growth of the service," a statement said.
In the statement, Silvio Scaglia, managing director of Omnitel, reiterated the company's aim of reaching 70 percent territorial coverage by the year end.
Omnitel Pronto Italia is 70 percent controlled by a consortium led by Italian information technology group Olivetti, and 30 percent by a consortium which includes Airtouch and Germany's Mannesmann.
Omnitel has said recently it expects to make a loss of around 600 billion lire in 1996.

The company said in the statement its interconnection charge with major European countries which it has to pay to state telecommunications holding Stet was more than double the European average of around 80 lire per minute.
"It is impossible to maintain competition if we have to pay more than 40 percent of our turnover to a monopoly," it said.

It called for a connection fee of 50 lire per minute and said if charges did not come down towards European levels "the concept of competition in telecoms will be compromised by our country." ($ = 1621 Italian Lire)
